message.content:
In most animal and plant cells, mitochondria are abundant organelles—often numbering from several hundred up to several thousand per cell, depending on the cell type and its energy demands. For example:

| Cell type | Typical mitochondrial count |
|-----------|-----------------------------|
| Neurons (high energy demand) | ~10 000–30 000 |
| Muscle fibers (especially cardiac) | ~5 000–20 000 |
| Hepatocytes (liver) | ~1 000–5 000 |
| Spermatozoa (flagellum) | ~50–200 |
| Erythrocytes (red blood cells) | 0 (they lack mitochondria) |

So while there isn’t a single “number” for all cells, you can expect anywhere from a few dozen to tens of thousands of mitochondria per cell, with the exact figure varying widely across tissues and species.
